recreational boater movement patterns were a better predictor than simple diffusion models of the observed zeb- ral mussel invasion pattern.

the spatial and temporal pattern of recreational boating activity is a better predictor of long- distance dispersal and invasion of aquatic species than simple diffusion models.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
recreational boating activity is the primary mechanism of long-distance dispersal of zebra mussels in Wisconsin.

the probability of long-distance boater movement is a function of the number of boaters in a county and the number of named lakes in that county.
The main takeaway from our work is that
recreational boater movement is a good predictor of long distance dispersal of aquatic species.
long distance dispersal events, though rare, can be important in the spread of invasive species.
long-distance boater movement patterns can be used as a surrogate for the spread of invasive aquatic species, and can be used to develop more effective management strategies.
